title: The Street Youth and the Generous Cook

keywords: story of the larrikin and the cook
full_text:
In the crowded food bazaar of Cairo, a hungry, ragged street youth named Salim spent his days lounging near the cooking stalls, begging for scraps and occasionally snatching a piece of fried pastry when the vendors turned their backs.

One afternoon, Salim approached the grand stall of Master Mahmud, the most celebrated cook in the quarter, famed for his roasted mutton and almond-crusted savory pies. Salim stood staring at the smoking grill with ravenous eyes, his stomach groaning.

Instead of driving the ragged boy away with a stick, Master Mahmud smiled warmly, wiped his hands upon his apron, and called out: 'Step forward, young man! Food is meant for the hungry, not for the display of greed.'

He seated Salim upon a bench, placed before him a steaming platter of spiced roast meat, fluffy saffron rice, and a bowl of chilled mint yogurt.

When Salim had finished every grain, he lowered his head, expecting the cook to demand payment or threaten him with the magistrate.

Master Mahmud placed a gentle hand upon his shoulder: 'Salim, you have sharp eyes and strong hands. Shall you spend your youth begging like a stray dog, or will you learn to build fires, knead dough, and master the spices? An honest trade is an armor that protects a man from hunger and shame forever.'

Tears of gratitude rolled down the boy’s cheeks. He knelt, kissed the master’s apron, and became his apprentice.

For ten years, Salim labored with devoted industry, mastering the craft until he became the chief pastry chef of the Sultan’s palace, never forgetting the generous cook who had offered him an apron instead of a blow.
moral: Kindness and practical mentorship transform an idle youth into an honest master craftsman.
